summary: Legacy supplier entity change caused invoice holds due to attachment filename truncation and PO-line allocation mismatch
description:
Issue summary: Several vendor invoices from supplier 'TriLake Systems' are stuck in AP hold. The invoice processor flagged them as potential duplicates and routed them to manual review. Finance reports these invoices correspond to open POs but are not auto-matching due to a mismatch between the PO's legal entity and the invoice 'payee' metadata after a supplier legal-entity consolidation last month. Additionally, OCR-extracted attachment filenames are being truncated to 64 chars by an upstream S3 metadata job which causes the duplicate-detection key to differ from the incoming invoice payload.

Impact: 8 invoices (total ~USD 42,900) are on hold and will miss the payment run if not cleared. Affected items are mid-month vendor payments with potential vendor relations impact.

Environment: Production invoice ingestion pipeline, us-east-1 region. Affected workflow: invoice-parse -> duplicate-check -> PO-match -> AP-hold.

Observed behaviour: The invoice parser extracts payee identifier that still includes legacy suffix (TriLake LLC) but POs are allocated to the merged entity (TriLake Systems Inc). The duplicate-check uses attachment filename+checksum as one of the dedupe keys; when the filename is truncated (by s3-metadata service) the key changes and the system marks invoice as 'new' but then fails three-way PO-match due to entity mismatch and goes into HOLD_DUPLICATE_REVIEW.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Upload sample invoice 'TriLake-INV-2026-0310-very-long-filename-that-exceeds-system-limit.pdf' to the AP S3 bucket in prod-us-east-1.
2) Let invoice-parser process (invoice-parser v1.12).
3) Observe generated invoice metadata in Dynamo table invoices-prod.
4) Check duplicate-check logs for dedupe key generation and note filename truncation.
5) Check PO-match service output and see mismatch between invoice.payee_entity and po.legal_entity.
logs:
invoice-parser logs (2026-03-10T14:12:23Z): INFO parsed filename=TriLake-INV-2026-0310-very-long-filename-that-exceeds-system-limit.pdf; s3-metadata normalized_filename=TriLake-INV-2026-0310-very-long-filename-that-exceeds-syste...; dedupe_key=sha256:ab12...
duplicate-check (2026-03-10T14:12:24Z): WARN dedupe_key mismatch for incoming payload vs s3-object metadata
po-match (2026-03-10T14:12:26Z): ERROR entity_mismatch: invoice.payee=TriLake LLC, po.legal_entity=TriLake Systems Inc
AP UI: HOLD_DUPLICATE_REVIEW created by rule po_entity_mismatch
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: 1) s3-metadata service truncates filename to 64 chars in metadata causing dedupe key drift. 2) Supplier consolidation updated POs to the new legal entity but legacy invoices still present old payee naming. 3) Invoice parser does not canonicalize payee names against supplier-entity alias table.

Actions taken so far: - Pulled sample object and confirmed s3 metadata 'normalized_filename' is truncated by lambda s3-metadata v0.9. - Queried supplier master data: supplier_id 7012 shows aliases ('TriLake LLC', 'TriLake Systems', 'TriLake Systems Inc'). supplier master has not been fully populated into the invoice-parser alias cache. - Temporarily added a manual alias mapping into invoice-parser cache and reprocessed a sample; PO match succeeded.

Open questions: - Should dedupe keys include checksum only and not filename? - Who owns s3-metadata lambda that truncates filenames? (tagged team: infra-storage)
resolution:
Workarounds and next steps: 1) Short-term workaround: Finance has manually approved 8 invoices for the current run (payment scheduled). Approval ticket recorded in AP UI. 2) Hotfix: invoice-parser will be updated to prefer content checksum + vendor_tax_id + invoice_number as primary dedupe keys (PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/invoice-parser/pull/312). 3) Medium-term: infra-storage to remove filename truncation in s3-metadata lambda and preserve original filename in metadata; change request filed. 4) Data: sync supplier alias table and add canonicalization rules for legacy entity names; ops task created to backfill supplier aliases for supplier_id 7012 and other recently merged vendors.

Planned rollout: PR for parser change to be merged after tests (target 2026-03-13), infra change scheduled with CI gate for 2026-03-18. Finance will monitor next two payment runs for recurrence.
comments: Ava Thompson (Support): Initial triage complete. Confirmed invoices on hold, extracted sample object and logs attached to ticket. Escalating to AP engineering and infra-storage.

Diego Martinez (AP Eng): I reproduced the failure locally. Invoice parser needs alias canonicalization. Created quick mapping to unblock one sample; will submit parser PR to change dedupe key order so we don't rely on filename. See PR link in related_github_prs.

Maya Patel (Infra-Storage): s3-metadata lambda truncation is an intentional historical limit (64 chars) set in 2019. I'll open an RFC to remove the truncation and keep original_filename metadata. ETA for change 2026-03-18 after infra review.
Liam O'Connor (Finance): We've approved the 8 invoices manually and scheduled the payment. Please flag if any more from TriLake appear in the next ingest batch.

Diego Martinez (AP Eng): Hotfix merged to staging. Will run a backfill job for invoices in HOLD_DUPLICATE_REVIEW that match supplier_id 7012 and TriLake alias list once infra approves metadata change.
